today_summary: GCM26 marked $3,864 with ATM IV 23.8% and a decisively call-heavy chain — 302,506 call OI against 114,439 put OI (P/C OI 0.38), though volume ran far more balanced at 6,281 calls to 3,572 puts (P/C vol 0.57). Net GEX within ±$200 of spot is -377, so dealers are short gamma right where price is trading and moves get amplified rather than damped. The 1σ daily move is $58 (1.50%), framing a $3,806-$3,922 one-sigma envelope. Max pain prints $5,225, +$1,361 (+35%) above spot and outside the entire ±20% chain window — it is anchored by 16,556 contracts of legacy call OI at $5,500 and should be read as a structural artifact, not a magnet.
five_day_thesis: Spot has lost $136 over five sessions (4,000.4 → 3,864.1, -3.41%) but the decline stalled: the last two prints were 3,853 and 3,864, a +$11 stabilization after three straight down days. The regime change that matters came on 2026-11-13, when window GEX flipped from +35.8 to -232.6 and has stayed negative four consecutive sessions — dealers went from dampening moves to amplifying them, which is why the 3.4% slide was orderly on the way down and why any break now travels further than the chain implies. ATM IV expanded +2.1pp (21.7% → 23.8%) across the window, peaking at 24.89% on 11-17 before easing, so premium got more expensive into weakness rather than cheaper — the opposite of a capitulation signature. Positioning rotated with it: call OI added +7,372 contracts while put OI shed -6,364, pushing P/C OI from 0.41 to 0.38, yet the put wall oscillated violently across a $400 band (3,700 → 3,500 → 3,900 → 3,500 → 3,700) with no strike holding more than 6,726 contracts, meaning there is no conviction floor being defended. Against that, the $5,500 call wall has not budged a single session, holding 16,547-16,556 contracts throughout — the only genuinely stable structure in the book, and it sits far enough above spot to be irrelevant to this week's tape.

prediction: Bias neutral with a downside tilt while spot holds beneath $3,900: the chain has no put wall worth defending nearer than $3,700 (6,070 contracts) and cumulative net GEX stays negative across the whole $3,095-$4,635 window, so there is no level inside the tradable range where dealer hedging turns stabilizing. Expect continued $58-per-day (1.5%) two-way range rather than trend, bounded by the $3,700 put concentration below and the $4,050-$4,100 shelf above, where per-strike net GEX first turns positive (+27.5 at $4,100) and call volume clustered 796 contracts at $4,050. A sustained break under $3,800 — where 620 puts traded against 31 calls, the heaviest fresh downside hedging in the book — reactivates the short-gamma cascade toward $3,700; above $4,100 the amplification inverts and the move extends to $4,350.
